notation.meaning: Regressors, coefficients and fitted values in the regression reading

blocks.md: A refresher, not a first course. It assumes Calc 2 and a first course in linear algebra, so it skips mechanics (differentiating, integrating, multiplying matrices) and goes straight to the results the MQE courses actually lean on — each one tied to where it shows up.

1. Open a unit and try its **Self-check** first; each question folds open to reveal the answer.
2. If you get one wrong or it takes more than a couple of minutes, read the linked concept note.
3. If you get them all, skip the unit.

| Unit | Topics | Needed for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Math Prep L1 Matrix Algebra Essentials](note:math-prep-l1-matrix-algebra-essentials) | Identities, inverses, determinants, partitioned matrices, trace | Every matrix derivation in [Econ 430 L7 The Classical Linear Regression Model](note:econ-430-l7-the-classical-linear-regression-model) |
| [Math Prep L2 Vector Spaces Rank and Projection](note:math-prep-l2-vector-spaces-rank-and-projection) | Column space, rank, orthogonality, projection | OLS geometry, identification, FWL in [Econ 424 L2 Between-Group Inequality](note:econ-424-l2-between-group-inequality) |
| [Math Prep L3 Eigenvalues and Quadratic Forms](note:math-prep-l3-eigenvalues-and-quadratic-forms) | Eigenvalues, spectral decomposition, definiteness | Second-order conditions, $\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}$, GLS later |
| [Math Prep L4 Multivariable Differentiation](note:math-prep-l4-multivariable-differentiation) | Partials, chain rule, Hessian, implicit functions, homogeneity | CES wages and the skill premium; comparative statics |
| [Math Prep L5 Matrix Calculus](note:math-prep-l5-matrix-calculus) | Derivatives of linear and quadratic forms | Deriving $\mathbf{b} = (\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{y}$ |
| [Math Prep L6 Optimization](note:math-prep-l6-optimization) | FOC/SOC, convexity and Jensen, Lagrangians, envelope theorem | Least squares, MLE, any micro or labor model |
| [Math Prep L7 Approximations Logs and Series](note:math-prep-l7-approximations-logs-and-series) | Taylor, logs and growth rates, L'Hôpital, geometric series | Interpreting log models and log gaps; Box-Cox; CES limits |
| [Math Prep L8 Integration for Probability](note:math-prep-l8-integration-for-probability) | Integration by parts, change of variables, Leibniz rule, double integrals | Expectations, lognormal wages, Gini integrals, LIE proofs |
The Concept Index lists a study order for every course; prerequisites from this course appear there in italics wherever an Econ concept needs them.

The first units build the tools a regression derivation needs. [Math Prep L1 Matrix Algebra Essentials](note:math-prep-l1-matrix-algebra-essentials) gives the rules for products, inverses, blocks and the [Trace of a Matrix](note:trace-of-a-matrix). [Math Prep L2 Vector Spaces Rank and Projection](note:math-prep-l2-vector-spaces-rank-and-projection) reads OLS as a projection onto the [Column Space](note:column-space), with [Linear Independence and Rank](note:linear-independence-and-rank) deciding uniqueness. [Math Prep L3 Eigenvalues and Quadratic Forms](note:math-prep-l3-eigenvalues-and-quadratic-forms) adds [Quadratic Forms and Definiteness](note:quadratic-forms-and-definiteness), which tells you a critical point is a minimum.

[Math Prep L4 Multivariable Differentiation](note:math-prep-l4-multivariable-differentiation) moves to calculus: partials, the [Hessian Matrix](note:hessian-matrix) and comparative statics. [Math Prep L5 Matrix Calculus](note:math-prep-l5-matrix-calculus) combines it with the matrix units to derive the OLS formula, and [Math Prep L6 Optimization](note:math-prep-l6-optimization) generalizes to constraints, with [Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multipliers](note:constrained-optimization-and-lagrange-multipliers) and the [Envelope Theorem](note:envelope-theorem). [Math Prep L7 Approximations Logs and Series](note:math-prep-l7-approximations-logs-and-series) covers [Logarithms and Growth Rates](note:logarithms-and-growth-rates) and the series behind interpretation, and [Math Prep L8 Integration for Probability](note:math-prep-l8-integration-for-probability) handles expectations, with [Integration by Parts](note:integration-by-parts) and the [Leibniz Integral Rule](note:leibniz-integral-rule).
Together the units run from algebra and geometry (L1–L3) to calculus and optimization (L4–L6) to approximation and integration (L7–L8), the tools the econometrics and economics courses use.
